newsitem.title: JAPAN: Bankruptcies abate in Japan but total stays high.
newsitem.headline: Bankruptcies abate in Japan but total stays high.

text.p: A wave of bankruptcies in corporate Japan has eased over recent months but a high number of smaller companies are still folding because of the sluggish economy, a research firm said on Tuesday.

In the April-September period, the number of companies filing for bankruptcy in Japan fell by 5.1 percent from the same period a year earlier to 7,187, the Tokyo Commerce and Industry Research Co said in a regular report on business failures.

The overall debt held by the bankrupt firms fell by an even bigger margin, suggesting that the bankruptcy problem is abating. In the six-month period, the amount of debt held by newly bankrupt firms totalled 2.9 trillion yen ($25.8 billion), down 39 percent from a year earlier.
The fall was fuelled by a steep drop in the month of September, when overall debt fell by 76.6 percent from the same month a year earlier to 428.9 billion yen ($3.82 billion).

The number of bankruptcies in September also fell 12.1 percent from a year earlier to 1,189. This was actually a rise of 5.4 percent from August, although the total amount of debt fell 18.9 percent month-on-month.

"Amid a growing mood that the economy is at a standstill, a conspicuously large number of bankruptcies was seen among small and medium-sized firms unable to adjust to the changing economic system," said the report, which covered only corporate bankruptcies involving debts of more than 10 million yen ($89,200).

The big decline in debt in September and the half-year period was because there was an extraordinary spate of failures in April-September 1995 prompted by the bankruptcy of an Osaka-based nonbank financial institution, Nishiki Finance Co, the research firm said in its monthly bankruptcies report.

Corporate Japan has been swept by a wave of business failures since the bursting of the 1980s "bubble" of inflated asset prices. The economy is recovering from the post-bubble slump with the help of low interest rates and government stimulus measures, but the improvement is still gradual.
Despite the fall in bankruptcies seen over recent months, a high number of companies are still going under because of the continuing sluggishness of the economy, the report said.
There were 688 bankruptcies caused by sluggish sales and other factors typical of weak economic conditions in September, accounting for 57.8 percent of the total number of cases.
Only transport and telecommunications saw an increase in the number of failures in September, with a rise of about nine percent from a year earlier to 47 cases.

Meanwhile, failures in the retail sector fell about 23 percent from a year earlier to 141 cases in September. The manufacturing sector saw bankruptcies decline by about seven percent from a year earlier to 253 cases.
In the six-month period, failures caused by weak economic conditions totalled 4,240 cases, accounting for 58.9 percent of the total. ($1=112 yen)
